Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government together with the community and Parents and/or families as well as private parties to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 14. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty. 16. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty. 16. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere. 17. Trafficking of women and children, hereinafter referred to as trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of women and/or children by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, falsification, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights. 20. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 22. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 23. Child-Friendly Regency, Sub-district, and Village is a Regency, Sub-district, and Village that has a development system based on children's rights through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Halfway house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26.

Article 35
The implementation of protection for women and children shall be carried out by cross-sectoral Regional Apparatus whose duties and functions are related to the protection of women and children.

Article 44
(1) Regional Governments are responsible for facilitating the availability of safe houses for women and children victims of violence.
(2) Safe houses aim to protect women and children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators and other parties.
(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) Criteria for women and children victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Article 11
The family, in efforts to protect women's rights, has the obligation and responsibility to:
a. protect women from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities to women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social affairs, economics, politics, and culture; and
c. prevent the occurrence of violations of women's rights in the household.

Article 9
Obligations and responsibilities of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. monitor the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children.

Article 41
(1) Health services as referred to in Article 36 letter b include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
(2) Health services for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty four) hours, with quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.
(3) Special health services for children victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.
(4) Women and children victims of violence have the right to health services, including:
a. medical services;
b. medicolegal services; and
c. psychosocial counseling.
(5) Comprehensive efforts to provide health services as referred to in paragraph (4), intended for victims of violence, abduction, neglect, economic and sexual exploitation, and trafficking in women and children, are guaranteed by the Regional Government.
(6) Comprehensive health service efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in stages adjusted to the regional financial capacity.

6.8.rationale: The retrieved English candidates already include the key provision: Pasal 46(1)–(4) provides “bantuan hukum” (legal assistance) for “perempuan dan anak korban kekerasan dan saksi” with a gender-responsive approach, and lists stages of legal process (reporting/BAP, prosecution, court examination, judgment, mediation, diversion). This is clearly about women’s involvement in legal processes (at least as victims/witnesses), which is typically what such an indicator captures. The judge incorrectly rejected it by requiring explicit coverage of women as suspects/defendants/perpetrators; that is an overly narrow interpretation given the text. Because the original Indonesian text supports a ‘Yes’ (women victims/witnesses in legal proceedings receive legal assistance), the golden label ‘Yes’ also appears correct; the error is primarily the judge’s reasoning.
